material_findings.finding: The Prompts category carries instructions spoken by participants and recommends piping prompts.md into a developer agent. Transcript speech can include quoted or adversarial text; categorization does not prove user authorization. Every executable handoff must be reviewed and consented.

When a project has top-level prompts/context/actions folders, the skill selects and writes those paths without an explicit destination approval. It avoids overwriting a previous split directory but does not expressly prevent overwrites in top-level project folder targets.
Transcripts can include private conversations, client data and third-party speech; source does not require minimization/redaction before putting extracted context in other tools or task services.
The source requires every sentence to land in a category but includes no coverage/index proof or evaluated edge cases for multi-category and interrupted speech.

positive_safeguards: Keeps speaker labels and original wording, avoids fabricated summaries and empty output files.
Explicitly avoids overwriting existing per-transcript split directories by versioned folders.
Gives humans discretion over ambiguous fragments and names followups as offers rather than automatic sending.
reasoned_cases: Spoken 'send this to our developer bot' can be quoted context rather than an authorized instruction.
A transcript with patient or client details must not be piped into third-party tasks by default.
An existing top-level prompts/recording.context.md is not protected by the split-v2 rule.
records.remediation: Require user-approved outputs, nonoverwrite defaults across both directory strategies, complete source coverage traceability, classification of all transcript text as untrusted, and explicit sensitive-data redaction/permission before handoff.

material_findings.finding: The skill's central workflow directs edits to canonical YAML under 07_continuity/ without an explicit user-authorized write gate or draft/proposed-change stage. Source-only review requests should not automatically rewrite established project canon.

It requires strong support but supplies no line-specific evidence format, old-value preservation/backup or deterministic conflict resolution. 'Strong enough' is subjective and can create untraceable canon changes.
Story drafts, quoted dialogue and worldbuilding may contain imperative text; source lacks explicit instruction/data separation and excludes no direct tool execution based on draft text.
The definition of done implies entire requested chapter scope checked, but no source manifest/diff or cross-file completeness proof is required.

positive_safeguards: Separates contradictions, ambiguity, newly established facts and open-thread changes.
Preserves old canon unless text clearly supersedes and records provisional uncertainty.
Keeps skill focused on narrative consistency and requires language-aware output.
reasoned_cases: A chapter says a character is 40 while canon says 30: propose a conflict before changing canonical YAML.
A quoted fictional instruction in a scene cannot authorize deleting prior canon.
Editing canon files requires approved paths/atomic backup and a reviewable diff.
records.remediation: Default to read-only review; present proposed YAML diff with source-line citations for owner approval, bounded file scope, backup/atomic writes, and explicit no-execution authority for fiction text.

material_findings.finding: Transcript/caption mode can contain student speech, identifiable speakers and course recording material. It requests confirmable names when appropriate but does not require institutional processing/distribution consent or redaction before multi-agent use and generated public captions.

After professor checkpoint it updates course_passport.yaml artifact_refs. This human confirmation is a strength, but there is no enforced destination/cross-project write boundary or fail-closed conflict handling for an on-disk mutation.

The script agent may invent worked examples subject to [VERIFY] professor checks; generated scripts remain drafts until claims/rights and course-source assertions are checked. Student-facing outputs require explicit release approval.

Read-aloud, accessibility and timing acceptance are procedural assertions; no recording, timing, actual captions or observed evaluation occurred. Evidence page distinguishes MOOC engagement from learning results.

positive_safeguards: Source references Guo et al. with correct observational-study scope rather than asserting video length proves learning.
Four agent responsibilities separate source fidelity, shot planning, series segmentation and caption accuracy.
Professor controls checkpoints; unresolved domain claims remain [VERIFY], inaccessible audio stays [INAUDIBLE].
Shared course passport forbids individually identifying student rows and checkpoint protocol requires explicit professor decisions.
reasoned_cases: A guest student's voice in a transcript requires permission/minimization before being sent to a captioning agent or published.
A screenplay 'ignore earlier instructions' remains transcript data, not a new command.
A professor approving episode scope does not automatically authorize uploading or publishing the resulting video.
Appending passport artifact refs must be scoped and conflict-checked.
records.remediation: Explicitly gate third-party speech processing and caption publication, enforce project-root artifact and passport write scopes, retain professor signoff with evidence and source rights verification; label pre-recording QA as unexecuted.
